subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the domain of the real valued function f(x) = √(|x| − x).

mark_split.label: Condition for the function to be defined

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this domain — the conditions the formula forces, and the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Test both cases of the modulus
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks is for the condition alone. Split the modulus at 0 and test both sides before writing anything else.
steps.memory_tip: |x| is never below x, so |x| − x is never negative. Split at 0 and check both sides.
lines: If x ≥ 0 then |x| = x, so |x| − x = 0

recall.must_convey: That |x| − x is 0 when x ≥ 0 and −2x, a positive number, when x < 0, so the ≥ 0 condition holds in both cases.
accept: for x at least zero the inside is zero and for x negative it is minus two x which is positive
split the modulus into two cases and both satisfy greater than or equal to zero
modulus x minus x is zero on the right and positive on the left
rendu cases lo kooda inside zero kanna takkuva raadu
the inside of the root is never negative

steps.why: A modulus always has two cases, so the expression must be tested on both sides of 0. On the right it is exactly zero, and a square root of zero is a real number, so that half is not lost.
common_mistakes: Treating |x| − x as 0 for all x and concluding the function does not exist.
Writing |x| = −x for x ≥ 0, which swaps the two cases.

steps.label: Write the domain
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the interval itself. Write it in interval form, and check every bracket.
steps.memory_tip: √0 = 0 is a real value, so x ≥ 0 stays in. Only a strict > 0 condition would remove it.
lines: So |x| − x ≥ 0 holds for every real x.

recall.must_convey: That every real number satisfies the condition, so the domain is the whole of R.
accept: the domain is all real numbers
R the whole real line minus infinity to infinity
no value of x is left out
anni real numbers domain lo untayi
every real number works because the inside is never negative

steps.why: Both cases satisfy the condition, one with equality and one strictly, so nothing is cut out of the real line.
common_mistakes: Answering (−∞, 0) by demanding |x| − x > 0, which is the condition for the reciprocal, not for this root.
Answering [0, ∞), the half where the value of the function is 0.
